affiliations.research_notes: The university is the best-supported named civilian employer at the time of the wartime torpedo work and OSS transfer. claims.claim_text: The indexed Carlo Calosi is identified with high confidence as Italian engineer Carlo Luigi Calosi, whom OSS transferred from Italy during the McGregor Project.
claims.evidence_excerpt: He was taken out of Italy ... by the OSS
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An institutional oral history explicitly links Calosi to an OSS wartime transfer, while Library of Congress authority and finding-aid data align the distinctive name with the Italian magnetic torpedo.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact indexed name, the explicit OSS transfer account, the Library of Congress authority form Carlo Luigi Calosi, and matching Italian magnetic-torpedo context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The oral history and naval-museum-association account place the transfer after the September 1943 Italian armistice; the NARA inventory identifies the November 1943 McGregor Project file.
claims.match_notes: Box 101 and the underlying McGregor file have not been reviewed, so the identity remains high confidence rather than confirmed. Later Raytheon roles are not substituted for the pre-OSS affiliation.
